title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 76
paragraphs: For when Cleomenes was consulting the oracle at Delphi, he was told that he would conquer Argos. So he led the Spartans out and came to the river Erasinos, which is said to flow from the Stymphalian lake — that lake, they say, empties into an unseen chasm, then reappears above ground in the territory of Argos, and from that point onward the Argives call the water Erasinos. When he reached the river, Cleomenes offered sacrifice to it. The omens were entirely unfavorable for crossing, so he declared that he admired the Erasinos for not betraying the men of its own country — but that the Argives would not escape him even so. After this he withdrew and marched his army down to Thyrea. There, sacrificing a bull to the Sea, he shipped them across to the territory of Tiryns and Nauplia.
